headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared file-based workflows; no direct data-egress path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman reads and writes project files like CLAUDE.md, memory files, and project notes, while pdf.js processes PDF files in browser-based tests. If caveman ingests PDF-derived text or notes from pdf.js through a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks a documented isolation/provenance layer, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF caveman consumes text extracted from PDF files without provenance tagging, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, file-mediated instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for PDF inputs and writing tasks.
Prefix all imported text with provenance labels.
Disable automatic ingestion of PDF-derived notes into CLAUDE.md.
Review shared files before caveman reads them.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are documented as network_egress:none, so there is no direct outbound exfiltration path in the profiles. caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while pdf.js touches PDF documents, but the pair does not show a shared OS workspace or third-party upload behavior. That makes leakage possible only through unusual local file sharing.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive PDFs into a shared local directory, both agents can access the same data class.
IF either agent is connected to an external uploader outside the profile, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of shared folders.
Use separate user accounts or containers.
Audit local file permissions before running either agent.
Avoid copying session logs into document-processing inputs.
requires-engineering: add explicit data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes project files; pdf.js also supports multiple instances but is a browser-based worker with only PDF-file I/O. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, git state, or shared OAuth scopes, so conflict is not default-dangerous. Uncertainty remains because shared filesystem layout is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF caveman is used to edit project notes while pdf.js writes derived artifacts into the same path, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one writer per folder.
Use timestamped filenames.
Check for existing files before saving.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman is a content-writing agent and pdf.js is a document-processing worker, so a plausible workflow is pdf.js producing extracted text that caveman then rewrites or summarizes. The profiles do not show a verification gate between them, so B may treat A's downstream text as authoritative. That is a default workflow risk, though not clearly action-taking or irreversible.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is fed directly into caveman prompts, errors can propagate without verification.
IF caveman's rewritten text is published or committed, downstream mistakes become visible.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require source-document citations in caveman outputs.
Compare extracted text against the original PDF.
Flag low-confidence extractions before writing.
requires-engineering: add automated verification of extracted claims.

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles do not document residency, certifications, retention, or regulated data handling differences. caveman touches session logs and project notes, and pdf.js touches PDF documents, but no compliance mismatch is evidenced. Because the rubric requires a concrete mismatch, this pathway is not established.
conditions: IF a regulated data class is introduced into either agent's workflow, a separate compliance review is needed.
IF residency or retention policies differ in deployment, reassess compliance.
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents.
Check retention settings before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review vendor compliance docs.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated data.
